plan: With uniform values on [0,49] and 3 bidders in a first-price sealed-bid auction, the Bayesian Nash equilibrium strategy is to bid (n-1)/n times your value, which accounts for competition while maximizing expected profit. With n=3 bidders, this means bidding 2/3 of my value. My value is $25, so I should bid approximately $16.7 to balance winning probability against profit margin.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the standard Bayesian-Nash equilibrium bid for a first-price auction is value × (n-1)/n = value × 2/3. This balances winning probability against profit margin, avoiding overpaying while still competitively bidding. Given my value of $18, I'll bid $12, which follows this equilibrium strategy and should maximize expected profit against similarly rational opponents.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, which is 2/3 for n=3. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $31, so I calculate 31 * (2/3) ≈ 20.7. Bidding this amount maximizes expected profit given the equilibrium strategy assuming other bidders behave similarly rationally.
